_notes: Single config for the response-only four-arm hardware campaign; campaign.py is the entry point.
Every relative path below is relative to defense4/timing/case4_architecture.
ARMS. The four arms share ONE build, one path and one endpoint fixture (same ports, same READ range, same
fixture delay). Two independent feature bits select them: T (timing) is a LIVE toggle on an installed
composite (hw/set_enabled.py, no reinstall); padding is a POLICY ROW, not a build property: the E table
Egress.conn carries an `enable` field written at install time from response_path_cp's pad_enable. The two
padding-off arms are therefore the SAME program with the padding policy row off, not a different binary.
BLOCKED (TODO, hw/ owner): hw/bringup_composite.py has no flag that writes pad_enable=0 (hw/rows.py calls
cp.e_conn_rows with its default pad_enable=True). Until the installer grows one (campaign.py looks for
`padding_installer_flag` below in the installer source), `run` REFUSES any arm with padding 0 and says so;
`run --arms size_only,combined` runs the two padding-on arms today.
BRING-UPS. N does not re-arm after a connection and a closed tuple sits in TIME-WAIT for 60 s, so a second
connection on an installed tuple fails. trial_mode per_trial_cold (default): EVERY trial is its own cold
bring-up (swap, restore ports, install, T, snapshot, run, snapshot, teardown) on a NEW master port taken from
traffic.master_port_range, incrementing per trial; arms that share a build still get a fresh bring-up per
trial. trial_mode one_connection: one bring-up and one connection per arm with reads_per_trial x
trials_per_arm READs (the persistent-connection mode). Cold swap, not a live re-install: the installer
refuses an existing manifest and a re-install on a dirtied daemon is unrehearsed.
BINDING. Each build's `hashes` are checked three ways before anything runs: config == the build's compile
manifest.json artifact_sha256 == the files under out_dir. A null slot is filled from the manifest; a
placeholder or malformed value is an error. endpoint.binary_sha256 / lib_sha256 cannot be derived offline;
they are pinned below and `run` re-checks them on Vision (command in `endpoint._pin_with`).
SHAPING. All hold-queue and blocker-queue rates default to 0 (unshaped, the production baseline). Set the
chosen rates here; the requested values are passed to the installer and to snapshot_counters, and the
ACHIEVED (hardware-quantized) rates read back in each snapshot are copied into campaign_run.json.
K. The installer's --k is 2*k generator tokens per trigger; production uses --k 2 (installer default and
hw/t_config.py pktgen_ops, count = 2*k); it is NOT 32.
Timing: readiness/cap sit above the fixture delay (5 ms) so the delayed child response arrives before the
readiness deadline and the normal commit/release path is observable (audit defect D).

production._note: The state observed before every run and restored many times on 2026-10-11. `run` reads the running program from ps before touching anything and refuses unless it equals `program`; the $PORT snapshot used for every port replay is TAKEN at the start of the run from that program (live_snapshot.py), never a stale file. Restore = cold swap to launch_script, restore_ports.py, switch_slot.py relay (if relay_slot), Vision restore, then the ping must succeed.

sbo_admission_01._allowed_loop_octet_gap_note: Per loop role (n_ack_return, t_in, hb_return, held_return): octets received but not in good frames that this build is allowed per trial. Default 0. The build before the RESET fix shows 80 on t_in; set {"t_in": 80} for that build only.

close_reset_fix_01._note: The build verified on silicon with the close and RESET fixes (loop-port gap 0), so no gap is allowed. sbo_admission_01 above is the pre-fix comparison build (known 80-octet t_in gap) and is validated but not used by the arms.

mirror_fix_01._max_token_stale_note: Bound on the OUT_TOKEN_STALE delta of a T-on trial (default 0). One of ~10 shaped runs showed 5 at a 3 ms fixture / 3,723 PPS; the T owner is analysing it, so raise this only deliberately. The observed value is recorded in every trial.
mirror_fix_01._note: Verified on silicon 2026-10-12 (evidence/mirror_fix_silicon_01): one READ trigger per READ, zero stale tokens, port gaps 0. close_reset_fix_01 and sbo_admission_01 are kept as named comparison builds.

expectations._note: THE one expectations table; checks.evaluate enforces it per trial from the trial's own evidence (before/after snapshot deltas, master.json, outstation.json, wire.json, timing.json) and a violation fails the trial. README repeats it. The T-on counts for the piggyback fixture are assumed equal to separate_ack (one commit and one release per READ) and have not been measured: only the fallback bound is restricted to the on-time fixture.

mirror_fix._note: Applies only to a T-on/T-off trial on a build flagged mirror_fix:true in `builds` (the builds before the compiler-mirror fix selected T's deparser mirror entry 0, giving several READ triggers per READ and thousands of stale tokens, so these counts do not hold on them; the check is skipped there). Deltas are after minus before from the snapshot pktgen block and outcomes. T1: READ trigger delta == READs; generated READ packets == 2k * READs (k = service.k, installer --k, 2k tokens per trigger); OPERATE trigger delta == SBOs run; OPERATE packets == 2k * SBOs; OUT_TOKEN_STALE delta <= the build's max_token_stale (default 0). T0 (as the T-off silicon evidence shows, evidence/milestone_sbo_01/toff): READ and OPERATE trigger and packet deltas == 0.

T1.note: OUT_TOKEN_STALE is bounded per build by builds.<name>.max_token_stale (default 0) and its observed delta is recorded in every trial.

arms.name: off
arms.role: feature-off baseline: composite installed, T off, padding policy off

service.note: installer --k is 2*k tokens per trigger; production k=2 (installer default)

shaping.note: Pick one with `preset` (or --preset). All rates are exact TM-shaper ladder values (the shaper realizes only 58/232/930/3723/14892/59570/238281 PPS; 0 = unshaped); any other value is rejected. shape_* shape the hold AND blocker queues together (measured 2026-10-11, evidence/p2_blocker_occupancy_01/STATUS.md: CLRT stays at the 0.8 ms target with unshaped precision and total passes drop 168-364x); slow_232 is a comparison preset only. block_burst null = installer default. Default stays unshaped until the lead chooses.

fixture.note: Two workloads, run and reported separately. separate_ack = vision_run.py casea on --delay-ms delay_ms (emulated relay: a separate ACK, then a delayed response, as the SEL-751 does). piggyback = casea off (the endpoint's natural ~0.3 ms response with the ACK on the response). readiness must exceed delay_ms + readiness_margin_ms or the delayed child response misses the readiness deadline (audit defect D); that is a warning. jitter is not implemented by vision_run.py, so any non-zero jitter_ms is rejected.

shape_14892_vs_3723._note: A paired block runs presets A and B (each its own cold bring-up) under IDENTICAL conditions {fixture delay_ms, READ gap_ms, start_delay_ms, seed}, alternating the order between consecutive pairs (A,B then B,A ...), and records each pair. Select with --paired NAME; the arm and fixture come from the block.

traffic.start_delay_note: maximum pre-connect delay in ms; each trial applies a seeded uniform draw in 0..N (seed = seeds.rng_seed + trial number, recorded). 0 = connect immediately.
traffic.master_port_note: Each connection gets its own cold bring-up on the next port in this range (N does not re-arm after a connection and a closed tuple sits in TIME-WAIT for 60 s). Pick a range not used in the last minute. range 8 is the 20-byte 8-bit-range READ profile.

loss._note: A preset is a list of {class, n}; `--loss NAME` runs one trial per entry per arm/fixture, each its own cold bring-up with `vision_run.py --drop CLASS:N` (classes and wire shapes: loss.py). The padded classes assume a padding-on arm; use the native classes (read_resp_native, select_resp_native, operate_resp_native) with padding off. max_recovery_s is the bound on recovery after the drop; exceeding it fails the trial, which is recorded and does not stop the campaign. n counts packets of the class on the connection (the handshake ACK is master_ack #1).

reconnect._note: c1 on the installed port, c2 from installed port + offset (no switch rows; must complete natively), c3 on the installed tuple again (recorded, not asserted). Run with --scenario reconnect.
